newsitem.title: UK: UK Co-op suspends two managers,opens investigation.
newsitem.headline: UK Co-op suspends two managers,opens investigation.

text.p: The Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) on Thursday said it suspended two managers and started an investigation into their dealings with firms controlled by Andrew Regan.
Regan leads investment group Lanica Trust Plc, which is reportedly interested in buying CWS's non-food business.
The two suspended executives are Allan Green, who is controller retailing of CWS, and David Chambers, chief general manager buying, marketing & supply chain.
"These suspensions arose from a suspected recent serious breach of trust," CWS said in a statement.

The co-operative added it had asked City law firm Linklaters & Paines and accountants KPMG to investigate "...business dealings between areas of CWS managed by Messrs Green and Chambers, and companies controlled by Mr. Andrew Regan in the period 1994 to 1997."
The group, which this week rebuffed Lanica's attentions, declined to give any further comment on the suspensions.
CWS, which said on Monday it had no plans to sell businesses to an "asset-stripping middleman", has operations ranging from food stores to banking and funerals.
